answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted with AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, Amazon S3 object storage used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption is applied by default at the storage layer. Engineers may not create production storage with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled, both before it is issued and at all times afterward. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically. If a laptop is not fixed within 3 days, it loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again. IT also keeps an inventory of all issued laptops that records each laptop's security status.

answers.reasoning_note: The current Endpoint & Asset Management Standard (KB-27 v1.2) answers this directly, and the Encryption Standard (KB-07 v1.3) agrees. answers.answer: Our documents do not say whether Tidewell offers a bug bounty program with rewards or payments to researchers. What they do describe is a vulnerability reporting process: customers and external security researchers can report suspected vulnerabilities to security@tidewelldata.example. Tidewell acknowledges reports within 3 business days and keeps the reporter updated during the investigation. Reporters are asked not to access customer data, disrupt the service, or disclose the issue publicly before it is fixed.

citations.passage: Customers and external security researchers can report suspected vulnerabilities to **security@tidewelldata.example**. Tidewell acknowledges reports within 3 business days and keeps the reporter informed as the issue is investigated.
Tidewell asks reporters not to access customer data, disrupt the service, or disclose the issue publicly before it is fixed.

answers.reasoning_note: KB-16 v1.3 (effective Apr 15, 2026) §8 describes how vulnerabilities are reported, but two searches found nothing about a bounty or rewards. A human should confirm whether a paid bounty exists. Don't answer "no" just because the documents are silent.

answers.answer: Our documents do not say whether the full penetration test report is shared, under NDA or otherwise. The Trust Center lists only a Penetration Test Summary Letter, which is available on request. That letter comes from Brightline Security, which ran the 2026 annual test, and gives findings counts by severity. As of May 29, 2026, it reports no open Critical or High findings.

As of the date of this letter, **there are no open Critical or High findings.**

answers.reasoning_note: Retrieved sources (KB-01, KB-17) cover only the summary letter, shared on request. No document says whether the full report is shared under NDA (only the SOC 2 report is listed as NDA). A human must confirm the full-report policy.

None of the retrieved passages mentions a SOC or 24/7 staffing. Related context: KB-06 §7 says automated detection rules send alerts to the Security team's queue, with high/critical alerts escalated under the IRP; KB-10 §6.2 sets SEV1 triage within 30 minutes. A human should confirm the coverage model.

answers.answer: Under the current Information Security Policy (v3.2), the Head of Security runs the security program day to day and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly. The CTO is the accountable executive for the program. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls and manages the SOC 2 program. Our documents do not name the person in this role, do not use the title CISO, and do not give the size of the security team.

citations.passage: **Head of Security.** Owns the security program day to day. Maintains this policy and its supporting standards, oversees risk assessments, leads security incident response, and reports on security posture to the executive team at least quarterly.
**Chief Technology Officer (CTO).** Accountable executive for the information security program.
**Security & Compliance team.** Implements and monitors security controls, manages the SOC 2 program, responds to customer security questionnaires, and supports audits.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer: KB-02 v3.2 describes security leadership roles but names no CISO or individual and gives no team headcount. Superseded KB-03 v2.4 and the 2024 answer library (KB-32 A-012) say the Director of Engineering owns the program. That is outdated and was not used.
